title: Optimal Trace Inequalities for Single-Shot Quantum Information
summary: Single-shot quantum information theory is governed not only by entropy exponents, but also by the finite-resource constants that multiply them. These constants directly affect the quantitative performance of decoupling, covering, convex-splitting, position-based decoding, and one-shot communication protocols, yet they are often inherited from nonoptimal scalar estimates or from classical-to-quantum lifting arguments that introduce additional losses.
